title: Same image, different mechanisms
summary: Change an image. Follow the numbers through silicon, then explore the anatomy of seeing.

input.label: Your image
input.description: The image supplies matrix A. A derivative filter supplies matrix B. CPU, GPU and tensor models calculate the same filtered output C.
input.scope: Filtering reveals changes in pixel values. It does not identify an object. The brain view is a source-guided illustration, not a calculation of your perception.

brain.label: Human anatomy · illustrative pathway
brain.scope: Highlights guide your attention through reference anatomy. Their timing, brightness and connections are illustrative. Unlit areas are not inactive.

stages.title: Find the visual landmarks
stages.text: Start at the occipital surface. This broad atlas grouping helps you locate visual anatomy; it does not resolve individual visual areas or predict a response to your drawing.

stages.title: Look across a pattern
stages.text: A human fMRI study found distinguishable responses to visual categories across ventral temporal cortex. Several anatomical landmarks are shown here to introduce that distributed organization.

stages.title: One region, many contributions
stages.text: The study's category information extended beyond the most strongly responding patches. A whole gyrus is not a dedicated face detector, and these highlights are not the original measured patterns.

stages.title: Ask what was measured
stages.text: The study measured fMRI responses, not individual action potentials. Follow the evidence to distinguish anatomical context, measured signals and the numerical filter running on the silicon side.

mechanisms.label: CPU
mechanisms.organization: A scheduler gives ready work to available execution resources.
mechanisms.state: Operands, partial results and memory contents
mechanisms.tradeoff: More execution capacity helps only when operands and independent work are available.
mechanisms.limit: A simplified work scheduler, not an instruction-level reproduction of a particular CPU. Model ticks are not measured chip cycles.

mechanisms.label: GPU
mechanisms.organization: Many threads perform related work; their memory addresses and active lanes matter.
mechanisms.state: Per-thread values, lane masks and shared memory resources
mechanisms.tradeoff: Regular work can fill lanes efficiently. Divergent paths and scattered accesses can reduce useful work per issued operation.
mechanisms.limit: This teaching schedule does not reproduce every GPU, or measure the GPU displaying this page.

mechanisms.label: Tensor accelerator / NPU
mechanisms.organization: A compute array reuses operands while accumulating a matrix result.
mechanisms.tradeoff: Regular tensor shapes expose reuse. Moving operands and handling incomplete tiles still cost work.
mechanisms.limit: A small generic array, not a model of a proprietary NPU. An artificial neural network is not a biological neural circuit.

mechanisms.label: Packet-switch ASIC
mechanisms.unit: Packets, lookup results and queue entries
mechanisms.organization: Parsing and match-action processing determine how packets are handled and forwarded.
mechanisms.state: Packet metadata, forwarding tables and buffers
mechanisms.tradeoff: A forwarding decision and an available output path are different things; contention can create queues.
mechanisms.limit: The switch example forwards data; it does not compute the image filter. ASIC describes a design category, not one universal architecture.

mechanisms.label: Human brain
mechanisms.unit: Biological signals studied at different scales
mechanisms.organization: Visual representations involve distributed, overlapping activity across tissue.
mechanisms.state: The atlas provides anatomical context; this guide does not calculate a neural state.
mechanisms.tradeoff: Different measurements reveal different aspects of the system. Regional fMRI patterns are not individual spikes.
mechanisms.limit: No equivalent CPU clock, FLOPS score, energy per image or predicted human response is inferred.

atlas.title: Allen Human Reference Atlas – 3D, 2020
atlas.finding: The reference provides anatomical labels from which doke's teaching surfaces are derived.
atlas.limit: These grouped surfaces are neither an individual's scan nor a measurement of functional activation.

vision.title: Distributed and overlapping representations of faces and objects in ventral temporal cortex
vision.finding: Category-related response patterns were distributed and overlapping; information remained outside the maximally responding regions.
vision.limit: The atlas highlights are explanatory landmarks, not the study's voxel patterns or an image-recognition model.

vision-timing.title: Speed of processing in the human visual system
vision-timing.finding: In an animal-categorization task with photographs displayed for 20 ms, a no-go-related ERP difference emerged around 150 ms after image onset.
vision-timing.limit: This is a task-specific electrical measurement, not button-response time, a brain clock or the timing of this guide. It does not calibrate a brain-versus-chip race.

bold.title: Neurophysiological investigation of the basis of the fMRI signal
bold.finding: In the studied visual-cortex conditions, local field potentials predicted the BOLD response better than multi-unit spiking output.
bold.limit: BOLD cannot be read as a direct count of outgoing spikes. The relationship depends on the preparation and measurement.

cpu-issue.title: The Issue Unit
cpu-issue.finding: BOOM's issue logic considers operand readiness and available execution resources.
cpu-issue.limit: This supports the scheduling principle. Doke's generic work scheduler is not a BOOM emulator or a timing model for commercial CPUs.

gpu-simt.title: CUDA C++ Programming Guide · SIMT Architecture
gpu-simt.method: Published GPU programming and architecture documentation
gpu-simt.finding: CUDA groups threads into warps; execution paths and memory-access organization affect how work proceeds.
gpu-simt.limit: This is documentation for a particular GPU programming family. Doke uses a reduced teaching schedule, not a device-specific performance prediction.

tpu.title: In-Datacenter Performance Analysis of a Tensor Processing Unit
tpu.finding: The original TPU study describes an inference ASIC with a matrix multiply unit and evaluates it on specified datacenter workloads.
tpu.limit: Doke's small tensor array illustrates data reuse; it does not reproduce this TPU or generalize its historical performance ratios to all NPUs.

switch-psa.title: P4 Portable Switch Architecture · version 1.2
switch-psa.finding: The architecture separates parsing, ingress and egress processing, and target-dependent buffering and queuing functions.
switch-psa.limit: It specifies portable capabilities, not the internal layout, latency or queue design of every switching chip.
